subject: Post-call: Performance & routing qualification + data residency constraints (Finexa)
messages:
From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Carol Tan <carol.tan@finexa.com>, Aaron Liu <aaron.liu@finexa.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 21 Nov 2025 10:12:00 -0500
Subject: Post-call: Performance & routing qualification + data residency constraints (Finexa)

Hi Carol / Aaron — thanks again for the demo earlier. Quick recap and next steps from our side so we’re aligned on performance targets and constraints you raised: 

Summary of requirements you called out during the call:
- Peak throughput: ~450–600 requests/sec for synchronous generative endpoint (95% of traffic in US East).
- Concurrency: ~40 concurrent active sessions per tenant; bursty spikes up to ~120 for short windows (30–60s).
- Latency SLO: P95 token-stream latency target <= 120ms in US, <= 170ms in EU, <= 260ms in APAC.
- Streaming behavior: incremental token delivery with first-byte within 200ms and subsequent tokens streamed continuously; ability to limit chunk size to 64 tokens on high-latency paths.
- Data residency: EU-produced customer content must remain in EU region and use customer-managed KMS; audit logs retained for 13 months.

Attached is a draft SLO matrix for Finexa (Finexa_SLO_Matrix_v1.xlsx) and the network path diagram you sketched (network-path-drawio.png).

Proposed immediate next steps (owners & ETA):
1) Marcus: run a short perf probe from our US/EU/APAC staging clusters to verify baseline p95 streaming numbers and return a short results table — due Mon 11/24.
2) Aditya: propose batching and quantization profile options that hit the throughput target while preserving median quality — due Tue 11/25.
3) Laura: coordinate procurement ask for the EU KMS policy and draft language for the DPA addendum — due Wed 11/26.

Questions from our side that will help tune the test plan:
- What percent of your requests are long-context (>2k tokens) vs short (<512 tokens)?
- Are there any geographic constraints for user auth/identity tokens (e.g., EU user tokens must terminate in EU)?
- For spikes, are they tied to specific customer events (e.g., nightly batch) or more ad-hoc?

If that looks right, I’ll schedule a 30-minute follow-up next week to review Marcus’s numbers and Aditya’s config recommendations.

Best,
Laura Bennett
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
laura.bennett@redwood.ai

From: Carol Tan <carol.tan@finexa.com>

Cc: Aaron Liu <aaron.liu@finexa.com>, Procurement <procurement@finexa.com>
Date: Fri, 21 Nov 2025 11:05:00 -05:00
Subject: Re: Post-call: Performance & routing qualification + data residency constraints (Finexa)

Thanks Laura — this is perfect. A couple of clarifications from our side: 

- Traffic mix: ~78% short requests (<512 tokens), ~20% mid (512–2k), ~2% long (>2k). Long requests are typically analytical queries and can tolerate slightly higher latency.
- Auth tokens: EU user sessions must be validated against an EU identity provider and cannot leave EU control plane boundary — but you can return inference results to our US services if the input originated outside EU.
- Spikes: Mostly ad-hoc (marketing campaigns), but we do see predictable nightly batch windows for some accounts (02:00–03:00 UTC) with sustained throughput for ~15–20 minutes.

We confirm EU KMS requirement and will share the procurement contact details for DPA language. Appreciate Marcus/Aditya taking the action items — looking forward to the test results.

Best,
Carol Tan
Head of Platform Engineering | Finexa
carol.tan@finexa.com
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
To: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>
Cc: Carol Tan <carol.tan@finexa.com>
Date: Fri, 21 Nov 2025 13:40:00 -05:00
Subject: Re: Post-call: Performance & routing qualification + data residency constraints (Finexa)

Laura / team — I started a quick perf sweep from our staging endpoints. Early notes (raw):
- US-East staging -> observed P95 streaming-first-byte ~95–110ms for short requests at 300rps with batching disabled.
- EU-West staging -> P95 ~150–190ms for similar load from EU probe (network variance visible).
- APAC (Singapore) -> P95 ~210–280ms depending on network path; larger variance on long contexts.

I’ll run the formal probe matrix that aligns with Finexa traffic mix (78/20/2) and include a 120s burst simulation to approximate marketing spikes. Deliverable will be a CSV with p50/p95/p99 and recommended model variant per region. ETA: Mon 11/24 EOD.

Quick recommendation based on initial sweep: enable small batching (batch window 5–8ms) in US to improve throughput to target without adding >20ms to P95; in EU consider regional model pinning with EU quantized variant to keep data in-region and reduce cross-region hops.

-Marcus
Principal Performance Engineer | Redwood Inference
marcus.lin@redwood.ai
From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>
To: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>, Carol Tan <carol.tan@finexa.com>
Date: Fri, 21 Nov 2025 16:38:00 -05:00
Subject: Re: Post-call: Performance & routing qualification + data residency constraints (Finexa)

Following up with initial config proposals after I reviewed the draft SLO matrix: 

Proposal A (latency-prioritized):
- Model: rdx-3b-quant-eu (EU pinning for EU requests) / rdx-3b-fp16 for US
- Batching: small window 5ms in US, 2ms for low-latency routes (APIs with streaming)
- KV cache: enable per-customer prefix caching for repetitive prompts (expected token savings ~12–18%)
- Streaming chunking: 64-token chunks; first byte target <= 150ms; continuous stream thereafter

Proposal B (throughput-prioritized):
- Model: rdx-3b-quant-highthr for US (more aggressive quant)
- Batching: 8–12ms window to achieve 550–600rps sustained with 300–400 concurrent workers
- Fallback: when regional queueing exceeds 200ms, route to a lower-cost variant in same region (no cross-region fallback unless explicitly allowed)

Notes on data residency & KMS:
- We can respect customer-managed KMS for data-at-rest in EU and provide per-request audit hooks. Tech contact: aditya.rao@redwood.ai for test KMS key exchange.

Next steps: Marcus will publish the probe results and I’ll pair with him to run a short AB test of Proposal A vs B on US staging to measure quality delta. If Finexa is comfortable, we can schedule a 45-min technical runbook session next Thu 11/27.

Thanks — Aditya
